newsitem.title: USA: FDA panel backs Stryker hip implant device.
newsitem.headline: FDA panel backs Stryker hip implant device.

text.p: A U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) advisory panel on Tuesday unanimously voted to recommend approval of a hip implant device made by Stryker Corp unit Osteonics Corp.
The Constrained Acetabular Insert is used only in patients who are at high risk for dislocation due to joint laxity, bone loss, intraoperative instability, or failed previous hip implant surgeries.
The agency is not bound by the panel's advice, but is expected to follow it.

The Osteonics device was originally approved in 1989, through the 510(k) process, which means that the insert was substantially equivalent to existing devices. In the early 1990s, some devices, including hip implants and their components, were reclassified by the FDA. The agency then required manufacturers to file a more detailed premarket approval application, including safety and efficacy data. Osteonics filed in November 1996, and presented data to the panel on Tuesday.

The company said that 1,457 inserts have been sold in the United States. The insert is only sold to physicians who justify the need for it, the company said. In two studies of inserts implanted in high risk patients, there have only been four dislocations after surgery, Osteonics said. Three reports of serious adverse events have been filed with the FDA. All were instances of recurrent dislocation.
Panelist David Nelson, an orthopedic surgeon, said that there "is adequate data in general to understand that these are safe and effective."
